A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with EO/SO renamed ePC/sPC in v3. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, linear and nonlinear MNIST convergence studies, and numerical-precision simulations. These appear in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a weight-gradient analysis in Appendix C.3 and Figure C.1.

M1.justification: EO becomes ePC and SO becomes sPC, but the procedures remain unchanged: zero-initialized errors, recursive state reconstruction, backpropagation through errors, and local weight updates. Algorithms 1–4 retain their substantive steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EMNIST-MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10/100, retaining the linear/nonlinear MNIST and easy/hard-input scenarios. The new gradient diagnostic uses the existing linear MNIST setup; probabilistic and continual-learning applications remain discussion rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The accuracy benchmarks retain the same comparators. In the added gradient-convergence diagnostic, Figure C.1 explicitly compares against backpropagation gradients alongside analytical PC gradients; v2's corresponding state-convergence analysis compared EO/SO against analytical state equilibrium.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an evaluation procedure tracking intermediate-step weight-gradient norms and cosine similarity to backpropagation in the existing 20-layer linear MNIST model. Retained experiments preserve their splits, preprocessing, architectures, training budgets, and hyperparameter values.

E4.justification: The new Appendix C.3/Figure C.1 examines whether PC weight gradients differ from backpropagation and how they approach equilibrium. Existing precision comparisons and nonlinear convergence analyses across losses and input difficulty are retained, with the latter moved from C.4 to D.2.

E5.justification: Accuracy tables retain means and standard deviations over five seeds, including the same documented seed sets. Figure 5 retains batch medians for n=64 with interquartile shading. The new gradient curves do not introduce repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the deep-MLP accuracy table are numerically unchanged. New Figure C.1 reports gradient trajectories that reach PC gradients distinct from backpropagation in direction and magnitude. The clarifying remarks also newly report ePC's 5–20% greater per-step runtime.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2.1 adds the explicit correspondence between one-step ePC with learning rate 1 and Z-IL. Appendix C.4 formalizes the Gaussian interpretation underlying the VAE correspondence. The existing equivalence theorems and binomial-to-Poisson derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain identifying exponential signal decay, introducing an equivalent error-based parameterization, accelerating convergence, and approaching backpropagation accuracy in deeper networks. Renaming, refined speedup wording, and shortening the contribution list do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation through new limitations and clarifying remarks on supervised-only evaluation, baseline selection, biological applicability, and parallelization costs. Appendix C.3 adds an interpretation of premature termination through gradient behavior, while Section 6.1 introduces a least-control perspective. Existing local-minima caveats are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v3 changes the advertised code repository from pc_error_optimization to error_based_PC and newly states a 5–20% per-step computational overhead. Its reproducibility statement points to largely retained details: hardware, architectures, seeds, sweep ranges, and selected hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Meulemans et al. (2022) and connects ePC to the least-control principle. It also explicitly discusses Z-IL using the already-cited Song et al. (2020) and expands the existing VAE connection. These are targeted positioning additions, without new empirical evaluations of those methods.

P1.justification: Beyond pervasive terminology changes, v3 rewrites and reorganizes the abstract, introduction, and background explanation. Appendix C is reorganized around algorithmic relationships, previous convergence material moves into Appendix D, and separate limitations, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: v3 adds the six-panel gradient Figure C.1 and speedup arrows and annotations to Figure 5. Figure 1 moves to page 2 and gains clearer axis labels; existing figures and tables receive renamed labels and revised typography. The nonlinear convergence figure is retained as Figure D.1.

improvement.justification: Figure C.1 supplies useful empirical support for the distinction between ePC and backpropagation gradients, previously addressed mainly theoretically. Clearer applicability limits and reorganized explanations also improve interpretation. These are bounded gains: the new diagnostic uses the existing linear MNIST setup, while benchmark results and core proofs remain unchanged.
